extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, funders, research administrators, and scientists interested in peer review and gender equity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating research grant applications to reduce gender bias by prioritizing the proposed science over characteristics or CVs of the applicant, and by using reviewer training to address unconscious bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the research rather than the researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Women lose out when reviewers are asked to assess the researcher, rather than the research, on a grant application. Female scientists suffer when their research proposals are judged primarily on the strength of their CVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize evaluation of the proposed science and the merits of the research plan instead of focusing on applicant-level metrics (CV, track record, identity). The study reported that when reviewers focus on the science, gender bias disappears; an anti-pattern is judging proposals primarily on applicants' CVs, which disproportionately harms women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train reviewers to recognize unconscious biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Training reviewers to recognize unconscious biases seems to correct this imbalance, despite previous work suggesting that it increased bias instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement bias-awareness training for reviewers as a means to reduce gender disparities in funding decisions. Note the caveat that prior studies have shown mixed results—training design and implementation likely matter—so monitoring outcomes after training is important.
